case_analysis.apparent_benchmark_claim: Move every song named in `~/documents/personal/songs_to_archive.txt` out of the user's Spotify playlists and place those songs into a new playlist titled `Old Songs`.
case_analysis.actual_checked_outcome: Released success was the conjunction `TestTracker.pass_count == TestTracker.num_tests` over seven registered tests: decoded task answer matches `answer.json` (`null`), `models.changed_model_names()` equals `{spotify.Playlist, spotify.PlaylistSong}`, exactly one playlist was added with no playlist updates/deletes, that playlist title equals `Old Songs`, the added PlaylistSong song-id set equals `private_data.to_archive_song_ids`, the deleted song-id set equals the same set, and the deleted playlist-to-song mapping equals `private_data.to_archive_playlist_id_to_song_ids` with `ignore_order=True`. The evaluator assigns `test.task_completed = active_tasks[0].status == "success"`, but that assignment is outside any registered test and does not enter `success`; no native test requires every added PlaylistSong to reference the new playlist or to appear exactly once per distinct source song.
case_analysis.target_construction_review: `Task.load` and `GroundTruth.load` bind the same task id to `specs.json`, `answer.json`, `public_data.json`, `private_data.json`, `evaluation.py`, and `test_data.json`. The loaded target artifacts are coherent for the released seven tests, but they do not define any separate native target for added-playlist binding or exactly-once insertion because the evaluator never asks for those outcomes.
case_analysis.evaluator_oracle_review: The official evaluator is a weaker operationalization of the apparent task outcome. It checks the song-id sets and deleted-source mapping but not that each added PlaylistSong belongs to the newly added `Old Songs` playlist, not that there is exactly one task-created PlaylistSong per distinct source song, and not `task_completed` as a scored condition. That is an evaluator/oracle measurement limitation, not a confirmed different-outcome conflict on these retained records.
case_analysis.reward_wiring_aggregation_review: No reward-wiring conflict was found. `evaluate_task` returns a `TestTracker`; `run_official_job` serializes that tracker and exposes its `success`; later join code reads `native_evaluator_output.json::tracker.success`; `Metric` only computes aggregates and does not alter any individual record's `TestTracker.success`.

official_benchmark_assessment.description: The native AppWorld evaluator under-specifies the instruction: it never natively checks added PlaylistSong playlist binding, exactly-once insertion, or `task_completed`; it only checks the seven registered outcomes encoded in `evaluation.py` and `test_data.json`.

checklist_and_case_packet_assessment.description: The frozen checklist and case packet preserve exactly the seven official registered tests and their conjunction, explicitly exclude `test.task_completed` from native scoring, and keep the added-playlist-binding and exactly-once gaps in `stronger` only.
